proposal.summary: Portfolio-risk's only winner with native execution evidence remains skfolio, but the pinned artifact (1.2.9, WalkForward source c99fcf71349e2df4a7a1033ee85ca2e9ced9abee, accepted 2026-09-19 per blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/receipt.json) is verified stale: upstream shipped six releases in the seven days to 2026-09-26 (v1.3.0 through v1.4.0 -- a live PyPI check run today confirms 1.4.0 is still current, nothing newer has shipped), and I independently re-fetched all six GitHub release bodies via gh api. Two are named correctness fixes to value_at_risk (integer tail sizes, v1.3.3) and EVaR (log-sum-exp numerical stability, v1.3.4) -- exactly the "deterministic numeric risk" measures this layer exists to supply -- plus a new GeodesicShrinkageCovariance estimator (v1.3.0) and a multi-period sample-weight fix (v1.3.2). However, I also read the pinned commit's own _walk_forward.py source directly: it imports only sklearn.model_selection, sklearn.utils, skfolio.typing and skfolio.utils.tools -- never skfolio.measures or skfolio.moments -- so none of the six fixes touch the code path this repo has actually accepted. The staleness is real and dated but prospective: it matters once (still fully untested) skfolio optimizers or risk estimators run natively here, which remains an open gap either way. No competing library earns a verified advantage over skfolio for the accepted role. Riskfolio-Lib's "lacks a walk-forward/CV harness" knock was independently refuted here (its own readthedocs course page teaches Walk Forward, Cross-Validation and Combinatorial Purged CV, confirmed by a direct fetch), but it still ships no GitHub Releases object, hasn't tagged in ~4 months, and isn't sklearn-Pipeline/GridSearchCV-native. PyPortfolioOpt, cvxportfolio (GPL-3.0, 14-month-stale tag), fortitudo.tech (GPL-3.0), riskparityportfolio (PyPI 0.6.0 has no matching git tag -- verified provenance gap, latest tag is only v0.5.1), OptimalPortfolios and factorlasso (real, current, but single-maintainer-concentrated -- OptimalPortfolios' own pyproject.toml confirms it depends on both qis and factorlasso from the same author) all stay source-review-only with zero native execution in this repo. Two capability-additive, lower-confidence finds deserve a bounded trial rather than displacement: pyhrp offers a second, independently-authored HRP/Schur-complement implementation (real tests, coverage, MIT) to numerically cross-check skfolio's own HierarchicalRiskParity output -- exactly the "independent reconciliation" this layer's language asks for and nothing currently supplies; riskkit-quant is the only candidate in the whole set whose stated purpose is pre-trade position-sizing/stop enforcement (confirmed via its own repo description and 13 real test files), directly on point for this layer's most-repeated gap, though at 3 stars/single-maintainer/no third-party adoption it needs its own proof first. No candidate reviewed, including skfolio at any version, closes the layer's core gap: a verified connection from portfolio/risk-measure output to NautilusTrader's deterministic pre-trade enforcement or broker reconciliation. That gap is unchanged by this wave and stays open.

winner_status.note: Pinned at 1.2.9 (WalkForward source c99fcf71349e2df4a7a1033ee85ca2e9ced9abee, accepted 2026-09-19) but verified superseded upstream by 6 releases in 7 days through v1.4.0 (2026-09-26; a live PyPI check today confirms v1.4.0 is still current). Two of the six are named correctness fixes to value_at_risk (v1.3.3, integer tail sizes) and EVaR (v1.3.4, log-sum-exp stability) -- this layer's own 'deterministic numeric risk' measures. All 6 release bodies independently re-verified via gh api against github.com/skfolio/skfolio/releases (v1.3.0 GeodesicShrinkageCovariance; v1.3.1 plot-crash fix + drops direct joblib dep; v1.3.2 multi-period sample-weight fix; v1.3.3 VaR fix; v1.3.4 EVaR fix; v1.4.0 plot_composition_treemap). A direct source read of the pinned commit shows _walk_forward.py imports only sklearn.model_selection/sklearn.utils and skfolio.typing/skfolio.utils.tools -- never skfolio.measures or skfolio.moments -- so the already-accepted WalkForward receipt (12 focused tests, 214 full-suite tests, 20 dev folds + 1 reserved period) is unaffected by any of the 6 fixes; staleness risk is prospective, mattering only once skfolio's optimizers or risk estimators (currently 0 native evidence either way) are actually run. No alternative library shows a verified advantage over skfolio for the accepted model-selection role. Recommend a pin refresh to 1.4.0, via the bounded trial below, before any further native acceptance extends into skfolio's risk-measure code paths.

challengers.name: skfolio (upstream v1.4.0, pin refresh of the incumbent)
challengers.why_better: Verified via gh api against all 6 GitHub Releases published between the current 1.2.9 pin (2026-09-19) and today (2026-09-26): v1.3.0 adds a GeodesicShrinkageCovariance estimator; v1.3.1 fixes a plotting crash and drops a direct joblib dependency; v1.3.2 preserves sample weights across multi-period portfolio updates; v1.3.3 makes value_at_risk consistent at integer tail sizes (correctness fix); v1.3.4 computes EVaR in numerically stable log-sum-exp form (correctness fix); v1.4.0 adds plot_composition_treemap. A live PyPI check today confirms 1.4.0 is still current -- nothing has shipped since. The two correctness fixes bear directly on this layer's 'deterministic numeric risk' requirement.
challengers.trial_plan: Reinstall skfolio==1.4.0 (tag v1.4.0) into the existing isolated venv recipe (blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/requirements.lock, regenerated with --require-hashes for 1.4.0). Rerun the unchanged evaluate.py --lean-source ... --out ... command, tests/test_research_evaluation.py (must still return 12 passed) and the full suite under the recorded SDK interpreter (must still return 214 passed, 0 skipped). Confirm plan_sha256, the 21 selections, the 6605 ledger records and all_training_exits_before_evaluation_cutoff=true reproduce unchanged -- expected to be a clean no-op since the WalkForward import graph excludes measures/moments. Then add one new bounded check outside the existing receipt: call skfolio.measures.value_at_risk and skfolio.measures.evar on the same frozen reserved-period returns sample under 1.2.9 and 1.4.0, and confirm the 1.4.0 values match a scipy/hand-computed reference at an integer tail-size boundary where 1.2.9 is expected to diverge. Pass = existing suite unchanged plus new VaR/EVaR values match the reference. Overturn = any existing test regresses, or the WalkForward source-hash comparison behavior changes.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none -- skfolio produces research-only portfolio/risk artifacts upstream of Nautilus; this layer's own catalog already states 'optimization and risk estimates are not pre-trade enforcement,' and no skfolio output is wired to the deterministic adaptive-paper engine, so a pin refresh cannot move engines-run/paper-acts-passed/paper-fills counts by itself.

challengers.name: pyhrp
challengers.why_better: Independent, from-paper reimplementation of Hierarchical Risk Parity (Lopez de Prado) plus Cotton's Schur-complement extension, with its own real test suite and published coverage report -- confirmed via gh api src/pyhrp/__init__.py exports hrp(), schur_hrp(), risk_parity(), build_tree(); tests/ contains real pytest content; MIT license; last pushed 2026-09-18. Not a general replacement for skfolio, but the only candidate offering a second, independently-authored implementation of the exact HRP method skfolio's own HierarchicalRiskParity estimator implements -- the 'independent reconciliation' this layer's requirement language calls for, which no reviewed candidate currently supplies for any risk-estimator output.
challengers.trial_plan: Install pyhrp==2.3.3 (PyPI, confirmed current) alongside the existing skfolio environment. On the same frozen SPY/QQQ/IWM reserved-2021Q1 return sample already used by the accepted research-evaluation receipt, compute weights from pyhrp.hrp() and from skfolio.optimization.HierarchicalRiskParity().fit() with matching linkage (ward) and distance settings. Pass = weights agree within a small numeric tolerance (e.g. 1e-6 relative), confirming both implementations compute the same method correctly. Overturn = a material weight disagreement not explained by a documented parameter difference, flagging a defect worth investigating in one of the two before either is trusted for risk allocation.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none -- a cross-check between two research libraries' HRP output, with no connection to Nautilus, the adaptive-paper engine, or any placed order.

challengers.name: riskkit-quant (riskkit)
challengers.why_better: The only candidate in the full researched set whose stated purpose is pre-trade position-sizing/drawdown/stop enforcement rather than portfolio construction. Verified directly via gh api the repository's own description reads 'A framework-agnostic risk-management toolkit for systematic traders: position sizing, drawdown control, stops, correlation limits, and a pre-trade validator' -- matching this layer's own repeatedly-flagged gap ('optimization and risk estimates are not pre-trade enforcement... no connection to NautilusTrader's deterministic numeric risk'). Confirmed real, not vaporware: 13 test files including test_validator.py, test_sizing.py and test_stops.py; PyPI requires_dist shows zero required runtime dependencies (only optional extras); MIT license; 30 commits, last pushed 2026-07-02.
challengers.trial_plan: Install riskkit-quant==0.4.2 from PyPI in isolation and run its own native test suite first (pass = its 13 test files pass unmodified, establishing it does what its README claims on its own terms). If that passes, build a small synthetic order stream shaped like the adaptive-paper engine's own order/fill records (not a live Nautilus wire-up) and run it through riskkit's validator/position-sizing API against the paper-e2e-20260921 receipt's already-recorded trades. Pass = the validator runs deterministically over that fixture and its accept/reject decisions are inspectable and reproducible. Overturn = its own test suite fails on install, or its validator's decisions cannot be explained/reproduced deterministically -- either would disqualify it from ever sitting near pre-trade enforcement.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none in this bounded trial (it only reads a synthetic/replayed fixture); a later real integration into the adaptive-paper engine's pre-trade path, only if this trial passes, is what could eventually move paper-acts-passed by adding a rejection path -- a distinct, larger step this review does not authorize.

researched_candidates.name: skfolio
researched_candidates.fit: Current pinned winner. On merit, not incumbency, it stays a strong fit: its sklearn-native CV/Pipeline design is the only candidate here purpose-built against the leakage/overfitting risk the layer's existing WalkForward receipt already exercises. But the 1.2.9 pin is now 6 releases/7 days behind upstream, and two of those releases are correctness fixes to VaR and EVaR -- exactly the 'deterministic numeric risk' measures this layer exists to supply -- so the pinned version likely carries now-fixed risk-measure bugs. No skfolio optimizer or risk estimator (only WalkForward) has retained execution evidence in this repo, and like every candidate below, it has no connection to NautilusTrader broker reconciliation or pre-trade enforcement.

researched_candidates.name: Riskfolio-Lib
researched_candidates.fit: The most-converged alternative to skfolio across every awesome list reviewed, and larger/older by stars and history. Its edge is raw breadth of risk measures and allocation models. Its gap vs. skfolio is architectural, not a feature count: it is not scikit-learn-Pipeline/GridSearchCV-compatible, so it lacks a built-in walk-forward/cross-validation harness -- the exact machinery this layer's only retained receipt (WalkForward) currently exercises. No GitHub Releases object exists for this repo (release history lives on PyPI/CHANGELOG only) and I could not retrieve CHANGELOG.md at the expected path to confirm 7.3.0's exact contents.

researched_candidates.name: PyPortfolioOpt
researched_candidates.fit: The most broadly cited classical baseline across the supplied awesome lists (5 separate list entries) and the largest community here (6,053 stars). Implements the efficient-frontier/Black-Litterman/HRP toolkit most other libraries in this set position themselves against. Release cadence is slower than skfolio/Riskfolio-Lib/quantstats (last version bump ~7 months ago) though commits continued through 2026-07-07, so it is maintained but not fast-moving.

researched_candidates.name: cvxportfolio
researched_candidates.fit: The only reviewed candidate whose core design is a realistic, transaction-cost- and market-impact-aware multi-period backtest simulator, mapping more directly onto the layer's 'reproducible equity accounting' language than pure optimizers like skfolio/Riskfolio-Lib. Local catalog (sota-convergence manifest, 2026-09-23) already carries it as 'not_individually_reviewed'/conditional with an empty evidence array; this is the first individual review. Under the strict 'no release or commit in 12 months' rule it stays out of the unmaintained flag only because of ongoing commits -- the release itself is stale. GPL-3.0 is also the most restrictive license among reviewed candidates.

researched_candidates.name: quantstats
researched_candidates.fit: Still the fastest-moving, most-starred reporting/tearsheet library reviewed, updated today. The repository's own critic (manifest-20260923.json) already flagged that no accepted receipt executes it -- an rg search over blueprints/evidence/manifests turns up only verdict packets and README mentions, no run -- and that gap is unchanged as of this review; quantstats' currency is not in question, its use in this stack is.

researched_candidates.name: fincore
researched_candidates.fit: The most substantive ground-up rebuild found for the empyrical+pyfolio+alphalens niche, with cash-flow-aware performance and capacity/round-trip analysis quantstats does not claim. Very new (5 stars) with a breaking 0.5.0 redesign, so no accumulated third-party adoption evidence exists yet -- capability claims rest on the project's own README (source_review), not independent usage.

researched_candidates.name: jquantstats
researched_candidates.fit: Directly targets a capability gap quantstats cannot fill by design (position-level, not just return-series, analytics) while staying a conceptual drop-in successor. Small community (45 stars) vs. quantstats' 7,658, so adoption evidence is thin, but the engineering (polars-native, typed, CI/coverage/OpenSSF-scorecard badges) is more current than quantstats' own tooling.

researched_candidates.name: ffn
researched_candidates.fit: Already named in the local catalog's own critic note (manifest-20260923.json) as 'the more current independent path' vs. empyrical-reloaded for cross-checking risk/performance metrics -- a judgment this review's fresher dates (2026-09-25 push) continue to support. Narrower in scope than quantstats/fincore (return/drawdown/stat helper functions, not full tearsheets or position accounting), so it fits best as a lightweight cross-check, not a primary reporting layer.

researched_candidates.name: fortitudo.tech
researched_candidates.fit: The only reviewed library offering Entropy Pooling combined with CVaR optimization -- a genuinely different risk-modeling approach (scenario/stress-based, not historical-sample) from the mean-variance/HRP/risk-parity families dominating the rest of this set. Smallest community (310 stars) among actively-releasing candidates. The GitHub tags listing returned an anomalous top entry (v1.11.12) that does not match the PyPI-confirmed 1.2.5; flagged as an unresolved versioning-scheme artifact rather than silently reconciled.

researched_candidates.name: riskparity.py (riskparityportfolio)
researched_candidates.fit: Purpose-built, academically-grounded risk-parity solver rather than a general optimization suite. The PyPI-vs-git mismatch is a concrete adoption risk: pip installing riskparityportfolio today does not get the 2026 commits, so this stack would need an install-from-source policy to use current code. Fit for a narrow risk-parity role only.

researched_candidates.name: pyfolio-reloaded
researched_candidates.fit: Still the most-adopted maintained continuation of the pyfolio tearsheet API and license (Apache-2.0). It is the slowest-moving of the actively-maintained candidates reviewed (no commit in over 9 months), trending toward but not yet past the 12-month unmaintained line; quantstats/fincore/jquantstats are all meaningfully more current for the same reporting niche. A fresher fork (quantrocket-llc/pyfolio, pushed 2026-09-17 per gh api) exists but reads as a platform-specific packaging fork rather than an independently distributed library.

researched_candidates.name: pyhrp
researched_candidates.fit: A focused, single-purpose, actively-maintained HRP/Schur-complement implementation positioned around interpretability ('explicit, inspectable tree') rather than breadth -- a genuine beyond-the-inputs find, not a re-surfacing of a supplied list entry. Complements rather than replaces skfolio/Riskfolio-Lib's built-in HRP variants; worth a direct numerical cross-check against skfolio's HierarchicalRiskParity estimator since both implement the same de Prado method. Small (55 stars), no independent third-party adoption evidence found.

researched_candidates.name: OptimalPortfolios
researched_candidates.fit: A single-maintainer (Artur Sepp) but extremely current, end-to-end pipeline explicitly covering rolling/point-in-time estimation through transaction costs and reporting -- closer to a full research pipeline than a pure optimizer library, relevant to the layer's 'reproducible equity accounting' language. Depends on the same author's separate 'qis' package for analytics/holdings simulation, so adopting it pulls in a second single-maintainer dependency. No independent citation or third-party benchmarking found beyond the author's own docs/CITATION.cff.

researched_candidates.name: factorlasso
researched_candidates.fit: The only candidate here with a citable, dated (2026) manuscript under peer review specifically describing its method plus reproducible replication material shipped in-repo -- the strongest evidence trail of any candidate for a specific numerical method (sparse factor/covariance estimation feeding risk models). Narrower scope than a full portfolio-optimization library: it estimates factor models/covariances that other tools (OptimalPortfolios, skfolio, Riskfolio-Lib) would consume as an input, not a replacement for portfolio construction.

researched_candidates.name: riskkit (riskkit-quant)
researched_candidates.fit: The only candidate in this whole set whose stated purpose is pre-trade position-sizing/stop/exposure enforcement with ready-made backtester adapters -- directly on point for this layer's own flagged gap ('optimization and risk estimates are not pre-trade enforcement... no connection... to NautilusTrader's deterministic numeric risk'). No Nautilus adapter exists; the listed adapters are backtesting.py/vectorbt/backtrader/freqtrade. Evidence maturity is the lowest here: 3 GitHub stars, an apparent single maintainer, no third-party usage or citation found -- claims above are read directly from the project's own README/badges, not corroborated externally.
